Answer: B
Reason: The frontal chest X-ray shows a right-sided, slightly lobulated mass in the superior mediastinum, and the lateral view demonstrates increased soft-tissue density in the retrotracheal space. These findings are characteristic of a mediastinal lipoma, which typically presents as a well-circumscribed, low-density (though appearing as soft tissue on plain film) mass that can extend into the retrotracheal region without causing significant tracheal deviation or invasion.
